rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an ML surrogate model trained on microstructural descriptors, while the paper used a physics-based screening of composition space (VEC, rule-of-mixtures modulus) to select a single alloy composition. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies standard tensile and fracture testing, whereas the paper performed room-temperature quasi-static uniaxial compression. The loading mode and test type are different, though both are at room temperature.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes nanoscale features governing dislocation pinning and crack deflection, while the paper's mechanism relies on reduced VEC lowering the Peierls–Nabarro barrier to promote dislocation mobility and delay cracking. These are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts faster and more accurate predictions of Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior, while the paper's outcome was a specific alloy with greatly improved compressive ductility and slightly reduced yield strength. The predicted property direction (improved ductility) is not explicitly stated in the hypothesis, and the testing mode differs.
